title: Responder Playbook: Ownership, Evidence, and Customer Comms for Multi-Tier Incidents
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook describes the end-to-end responder workflow for multi-tier incidents affecting Redwood inference services (hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments). It codifies:
- role assignment and ownership (First Responder, Bridge Operator, Evidence Scribe, Service Steward)
- required evidence capture and artifact templates
- escalation matrix and thresholds for P0/P1/P2 incidents
- customer-facing status templates and cadence
- fair on-call rotation, handoff, and game day exercises to validate readiness

Purpose and audience

Purpose: Provide a single, actionable reference that responders, on-call engineers, and support leads can follow during incidents to minimize time-to-recovery, preserve forensic evidence for postmortem/regulatory needs, and keep customers informed.
Audience: SREs, Serving Runtime engineers, Support, Solutions, and Customer Success.

Scope

This playbook covers multi-tier incidents that: degrade latency or availability for production inference (including model quality regressions that materially increase error rates). It does NOT replace service-specific runbooks (see "Systems and Services" index) but provides the orchestration and communication layer for cross-service events.

Definitions and severity thresholds

- P0 (SEV0): Total service outage for a region or Dedicated pool; >99% customer impact on requests; estimated MTTR > 30 minutes. Immediate exec notice.
- P1 (SEV1): Large degraded availability or latency impacting >10% of requests or high error-rate regression tied to model serving logic. 15–60 minute MTTR objective.
- P2 (SEV2): Non-critical but customer-visible degradation (rate limits, partial feature loss). 4–24 hour MTTR objective.
- P3 (SEV3): Low-impact issues or maintenance windows. Documented in weekly ticketing.

SLOs and alert thresholds (example)

- Hosted API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly.
- Latency SLO (tail): p99 <= 750ms for 1k token requests. Alert if p99 > 900ms for 5 minutes.
- Error-rate SLO: 0.5% overall error rate. Alert if error-rate > 1% over 5m or if model hallucination detection increases by >3x baseline on quality signals.

Detection signals (signals that often trigger multi-tier incidents)

- Sudden p99 latency spikes correlated across model endpoints and regions.
- Queue/backlog growth at the serving runtime or batching router.
- Rapid KV cache eviction rates with corresponding latency climbs.
- Autoscaling throttle / GPU OOM patterns visible in fleet metrics.
- Customer tickets describing silent failures or truncated streaming responses.

Initial triage checklist (first 10 minutes)

1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and create the incident channel (Zoom/Slack bridge). Assign roles explicitly:
   - First Responder (FR): primary investigator (typically service owner).
   - Bridge Operator (BO): runs the incident bridge, controls status cadence.
   - Evidence Scribe (ES): captures artifacts and timestamps (see Evidence template).
   - Service Steward (SS): coordinates customer comms and business impacts.
2) Record initial state: time, alert source, immediate symptoms, affected regions, sample request IDs.
3) Run quick sanity checks: cluster health, GPU utilization, queue depths, model process restarts, recent deploys/rollouts.
4) If P0/P1 suspected, notify on-call lead and exec DSP (follow Exec Notify SOP).

Evidence capture (Evidence Scribe responsibilities)

The Evidence Scribe is mandatory for P0/P1 incidents. The ES must collect:
- Short textual timeline of events (ISO8601 timestamps).
- Key metric snapshots (p99 latency, error rate, queue depth) for 5m/15m/1h windows.
- Relevant logs and stack traces (service name, time window, and request IDs). Example CLI snippet:
```bash
# Example: fetch fleet metrics for last 15m
redwood-metrics query --service=serving-runtime --metric=p99_latency --from=15m --format=json > p99_15m.json
```
- Captured coredumps or GPU driver logs (if present).
- Model checksum and version used by affected nodes (git sha or model registry id).
- Any configuration changes or rollouts in the preceding 30 minutes.

Store artifacts in the incident evidence bucket: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/. Ensure retention flags are set for regulatory incidents (30–90 days depending on severity).

Escalation matrix (condensed)

- If First Responder cannot identify a root cause within 20 minutes for P0, escalate to Senior SRE and Eng Manager.
- For P1, escalate at 45 minutes if MTTR estimate > 60 minutes.
- For cross-regional capacity failures, engage Capacity and Cloud Networking on-call immediately.

Table (text) — Example routing by symptom:

Symptom -> Primary Owner -> Secondary
- KV cache evictions -> Serving Runtime -> Model Onboarding
- Autoscaler stampede -> GPU Fleet -> Cloud Infra
- Model quality regression -> Applied ML + Model Onboarding -> Serving Runtime

Containment and mitigation patterns (common quick fixes)

- Switch traffic to healthy region or Dedicated pool variant (routing policy).
- Roll back recent model or infra rollout via the Canary rollback procedure.
- Reduce batch sizes or enable conservative batching policy to alleviate queue growth.
- Drop non-essential telemetry/ingest to recover headroom.

Customer communication templates (Service Steward owns cadence)

Internal status cadence (example)
- Every 5m for P0 until stable.
- Every 15m for P1.
- Every 60m for P2 until resolved.

External (customer) status template — initial notice (30 minutes):

Subject: [Redwood] Degradation impacting inference in region {region} — {short-impact}

Body:
We are investigating elevated latency and request errors impacting inference for customers in {region}. Our on-call team has opened incident {incident-id} and is actively triaging. We will provide an updated status at {time+30m}.
Impacted features: {features}
Workaround: {workaround or "none known"}
Contact: support@redwood.ai or your account rep.

Follow-up template (every update):
- Summary of work performed in last interval
- Observed effect on metrics (p99 latency, error rate)
- Next steps and estimated time to next update

Final closure template: acknowledgement of outage, root cause summary, remediation steps taken, and SLA credit guidance if applicable. Include link to postmortem when published.

On-call rotation and fairness rules

- Default shift: 1 week (Mon 08:00 local -> Mon 08:00 local) for platform SREs; exceptions allowed with manager approval.
- Swap window policy: swaps must be logged in the oncall-rota spreadsheet and approved by swap partner 24h in advance unless emergency.
- Maximum consecutive on-call weeks: 3. After 3 weeks, a rest week with no pager is required.
- Protected time: no major releases or mandatory training scheduled during the primary on-call week unless mutually agreed.

Handoff checklist (to be executed during the 15-minute overlap)

- Outgoing FR summarizes open incidents and evidence bucket locations.
- Confirm known mitigations and least-stable services.
- Hand off any in-progress customer comms drafts.
- New FR repeats back summary and acceptance of ownership.

Game day (simulation) curriculum — 90 minute template

Objective: Validate responder choreography for a cascading KV cache eviction that leads to routing fallback and a regional capacity spike.

Pre-Game Steps:
- Schedule participants: FR, BO, ES, SS, Capacity on-call.
- Freeze the incident evidence bucket and create a game-day incident-id.
- Prepare synthetic traffic generator with request patterns that exercise prefix cache hits/misses.

Exercise script (90 minutes):
- 0–10m: Inject synthetic cache-eviction event and open bridge.
- 10–25m: Observe queue growth; validate that FR runs triage checklist and captures metrics.
- 25–40m: Introduce model rollout event (simulated) to test rollback path.
- 40–60m: Force region failover (traffic routing change) and confirm customer comms flow.
- 60–80m: Stabilize and collect evidence.
- 80–90m: Rapid postmortem micro-retro (what went well, what broke, action owners).

Success criteria:
- Evidence Scribe collected required artifacts within 20 minutes.
- Bridge Operator executed customer comm cadence without missed updates.
- Rollback path executed within SLA for rollout mitigations.

Postmortem and remediation process

- Postmortem draft must be produced within 5 business days for P0/P1; 10 business days for P2. Use the incident postmortem template.
- Postmortem must include: timeline, root cause analysis, action items (owner + due date), verification plan, and whether incident evidence will be archived for compliance.
- Action items are tracked in the Incident Action Tracker board; responsible owners must add verification comments when complete.

Runbook lifecycle and governance

- Runbooks reviewed quarterly by owning teams. After any incident where a runbook was used, update the runbook within 7 days with lessons learned and annotated timestamps.
- The Evidence Scribe tags runbooks used in the incident artifact metadata (runbook-id).

Appendices

A) Evidence capture template (text)
- Incident ID: {incident-id}
- Timeline (ISO8601):
  - T0: {timestamp} — alert triggered
  - T1: {timestamp} — bridge opened
  - T2: {timestamp} — mitigations applied
- Key metrics snapshot filenames: p99_5m.json, errors_15m.csv
- Logs saved: serving-runtime-logs-{start}-{end}.tgz
- Model version: {model-registry-id}
- Notable changes in last 30 minutes: {deploys/configs}

B) Minimal CLI checklist for common evidence collection
```bash
# Grab recent fleet events and upload to evidence bucket
redwood-events export --from=30m --to=now --service=serving-runtime | gzip > events_30m.json.gz
aws s3 cp events_30m.json.gz s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/
```

C) Post-incident verification (sample)
- Confirm p99 latency returns under SLO for 24h.
- Run synthetic canary traffic for 4 hours to show stable behavior.
- Close action items only after verification comments are present.

Contacts and escalation phone list (text)
- Serving Runtime on-call: pager (see PagerDuty) and slack @serving-runtime-oncall
- Capacity on-call: pager and slack @capacity-oncall
- Product/Account escalation: account-ops@redwood.ai

Document maintenance

Owner: SRE Team (oncall working group).
Next review date: 2026-09-15.

If you find gaps in this playbook during an incident or game day, raise an issue in the Runbook Improvements board and tag @oncall-runbook-maintainers.

End of playbook
